pass_a_gloss: word rebukes not the things practiced from God—may it not be—as God’s; because they were not making the foretelling free of a lie. Yet since not having taken from truth they speak whatever they should wish, in this at least they have also missed according to themselves. Palladius: Will we then in this discern whether God is the one giving oracles, or then those ones speak their own things? Cyril: Very much; for a divine nomos / law will also straightway persuade us unto this. For God said thus in Deuteronomy: ‘And if someone should say in a heart: How will we know the word which the Lord has not spoken? as many as that prophet should speak upon the Lord’s name, and the word should not come to be which the Lord has not spoken, in impiety the prophet has spoken; you will not hold off from him.’ You hear that he says the failures in the things foretold will be a clear demonstration of something not having been oracled from God? for the truth loves truth. Some such thing he says through Jeremiah’s voice: ‘I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God from far; if a human will be hidden in hidden places, will I not also see him? Do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord. Have I heard what the prophets speak—false things which the prophets prophesy in my name?’ Then through the middle having accused not a little those who have despised the divine nomoi / laws, he gives the truth as a clear demonstration of both the things from God and not. For he said again: ‘The prophet in whom is his dream, and in whom is my word toward him, let him narrate my word upon truth.’ As if something should appear having missed the truth, it would show at once its begetter false-speaking, and speaking from his own heart, not from the Lord’s mouth, according as it has been written. Palladius: Do you wish we should set something of the necessary things unto a test, or leaving it go wherever your word should carry us? Cyril: And indeed, Palladius, of the necessary things unto benefit our word is not short; as for not saying the seeming freely I would accuse, and very reasonably; speak then having hesitated at nothing. Palladius: If some do not speak from the Lord’s mouth, yet belch, as you say, the things from a heart, in what manner then did that ventriloquist woman bring forward holy Samuel already dead to Saul, clarifying for him the end of the things about to be for him? for some think these things have been done thus, and not otherwise. Cyril: And do you yourself think it does not hold thus, and will you reckon this better, or then do you say emptily that the righteous one’s soul was truly forced out, and came when a little woman was calling?
